description:
FILED s477 (Fable, 2026-09-08) from the s473b review probes.  PRE-EXISTING: identical on main c8d11c31 and on the s473b tree 3b153d7f.  NOT the #1241 family (which is about the CONTAINER of a subscript, i.e. intermediate levels -- those now match perl); this is the rvalue CAST of the LAST level.

Reproducer (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL):
  my %sc; my $cnt = eval { scalar @{$sc{a}{b}} } // "died";
  print ref($sc{a}), " ", (defined $sc{a}{b} ? ref($sc{a}{b}) : "undef"), " $cnt";
      # perl (use strict):     HASH undef died        <- $sc{a} IS vivified (container), $sc{a}{b} is NOT, the cast dies
      # perl (no strict refs): HASH undef 0           <- @{undef} reads @{""}, element left undef
      # PCL (both):            HASH ARRAY 0           <- PCL vivifies $sc{a}{b} into an array ref

Rule (perlref, "Using References"): an RVALUE dereference of undef never autovivifies -- only LVALUE contexts (assignment, push, foreach alias, sub args, `\@{...}`) do.  PCL's `p-cast-@` reaches the vivifying chain walker for an element operand on the read path too.

Relation: PCL does not model `use strict refs` (docs/not-supported.md "use strict refs is not enforced"), so the die half is out of scope; the divergence to fix is the VALUE half -- the element must stay undef and the read must answer the empty list.  Discriminate first: which cast sites (`@{ELEM}`, `%{ELEM}`, `scalar @{...}`, `keys %{...}`, `@{ELEM}[...]`) take the vivifying walker on a pure read, and which perl consumers of the cast ARE lvalue (push @{$h{a}{b}}, foreach (@{$h{a}{b}}), `\@{...}`, sub args) and must keep vivifying.  Probe each vs perl under `no strict refs` before touching the walker; a fix that stops `push @{$h{a}{b}}, 1` from vivifying is worse than the bug.  Guard rows in Pl/t/autoviv-02.t both ways (rvalue does not create, lvalue consumers do), inverse-verified.  Bars: an emission change is likely -> gen bump + corpus-diff + emission-ab + sweep.
subject: An RVALUE `@{ $h{a}{b} }` / `scalar @{ELEM}` deref of an UNDEF element VIVIFIES the element into an array; perl dies under strict refs ("Can't use an undefined value as an ARRAY reference") and under no strict leaves it undef (reads the empty array named "")
